findings.reason: the plan already paid for this defect once (§53 was given a wait on §54 by review) and without the edge a dispatch of §55 lands on a file a live §53 node owns.
findings.text: §55 writes `reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py` while §53 does too, and the document's `plan-section-depends-on` declares no edge for §55, so both sections read as ready and two nodes can edit `_reserved_lane_exclusion` and `candidates()` concurrently

findings.reason: a node confined to the declared write paths has no field to express the deliverable in, and the literal reading inverts its outcome.
findings.text: the deliverable says "the candidate carries a reason naming the waiver", but `reasons` is the exclusion channel: `_pick` splits `offered = [c for c in options if not candidate.reasons]` (reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:399), so a waiver written there turns the offered lane back into the refusal the section exists to remove, and `reckon/crew/picker/types.py`, where a note field would be — `Candidate` has no other per-candidate string channel (types.py:26–84) — is not among the section's write paths

findings.reason: named the caller and the two-pass placement, a node implements it directly; unnamed, it must discover the same facts and may try to evaluate the condition inside a function that structurally cannot.
findings.text: the waiver fires "when every candidate that no reserved-lane policy covers is excluded on context-fit", a fact about the whole scan, but the section locates the reserved-lane policy in `_reserved_lane_exclusion` (snapshot.py:1186), which receives one candidate's `declared`, `attempts` and `utilisation` and cannot see the others; the caller that holds the set, `candidates` (snapshot.py:1316, which computes the reserved-lane exclusion at :1617 before `_fit` at :1636), is named nowhere in the section

findings.reason: the waiver changes lane eligibility for every pick, so a gate that never runs the existing picker tests cannot show the change left other picks where they were, and §52–§54 already state the base-arm arm this section omits.
findings.text: §55's gate runs only `tests/test_an_oversize_node_reaches_a_reserved_lane.py`, with no base arm and no existing test file named, although the section edits `candidates()` on the picker's hot path and nineteen test files import `reckon.crew.picker.snapshot`

findings.reason: adding fields to the timing row is exactly what those files read, and with no arm over them a node can satisfy its own case while changing the record an existing test asserts.
findings.text: §56's gate runs only its new file, though it edits `_record_pick_timings` (reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:98), which six existing test files exercise, among them `tests/test_pick_records_its_stage_times.py` and `tests/test_hold_records_its_state.py`

findings.reason: the prefix rule is mechanical and a node derives the code from the reason text, so only the illustration and a test written from it would be wrong, not the mechanism.
findings.text: §56 lists `budget` among the reason codes, but the budget gate emits `budget-ceiling:` (reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:1178, :1185) and two reasons carry no colon at all (`review-excluded-backend` at :1523, `in-harness-backend` at :1530), so neither the example code nor a bare `split(":")[0]` on such a reason yields what the sentence implies

response_events.reason: §53 has no live request and no builder, so a declared wait would hold §55 indefinitely; if §53 is dispatched while §55 runs, the dispatch scope check refuses the second claimant on snapshot.py, so the two cannot edit it concurrently

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §55 and §56 each gate on their new test alone, naming neither the existing test files covering the edited module nor a base arm, against the plan's own convention in §52/§53/§54.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — neither section names a scratch or node-local path; their write paths are repository source plus the new test, and the run-directory log convention from §52–§54 carries.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the two new test filenames and the symbols they name describe the mechanism, with no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §55's waiver is a condition over the whole candidate set, evaluated by a channel and in a function the section's own text cannot support.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §55 carries one deliverable (waive the reserved lane's tier and attempts terms for an oversize node) and §56 one (record a refusal's exclusions), and the document metadata agrees with the forty-eight done sections.
